entries.summary: Proof/show needs complete reasoning and explicit conclusion
entries.verbatim_extracted_excerpt:
Candidates must be informed that if the question requires to show/prove something, the conclusion must always be
stated again.
It is important that candidates understand how to approach the “hence” part of a question.
Calculator and arithmetic skills of many candidates are not up to standard.
entries.limit: Reported cohort difficulty; not diagnosis of an individual learner and not an invented distractor rationale

entries.summary: A plotted coordinate is not automatically the transformed graph intercept
entries.verbatim_extracted_excerpt:
Many candidates, wrongly used 1.693 as the y-intercept. Candidates did not realise that they the value
             of the y-intercept had to be calculated by substituting one of the two coordinates into the straight-line
             formula.  Some  candidates  also  did  not  realise  that  1.169  is  a  ln  y-value.  They  wrongly  substituted  it
             as ln 1.169.
entries.limit: Reported cohort difficulty; not diagnosis of an individual learner and not an invented distractor rationale

entries.summary: There is no universal quotient rule for integration; use the algebraic quotient first
entries.verbatim_extracted_excerpt:
Most candidates wrongly attempted to apply a quotient rule in integration.
                Very     few     correct     solutions     were     seen.     It     seemed     as     if     the     majority     of     the     candidates      were     never
                exposed to a similar question in the past.
entries.limit: Reported cohort difficulty; not diagnosis of an individual learner and not an invented distractor rationale

entries.summary: Perpendicularity requires the scalar product to equal zero
entries.verbatim_extracted_excerpt:
A few candidates calculated a scalar product but did not equate it to zero. This could not be accepted
            because the concept of perpendicular vectors is based on the scalar product being equal to zero.
entries.limit: Reported cohort difficulty; not diagnosis of an individual learner and not an invented distractor rationale

entries.summary: Compare trapezium chords with curve to justify estimate bias
entries.verbatim_extracted_excerpt:
Candidates must be taught to draw straight lines between two points on the graph to decide whether it is an
            over- or under estimate. It is not advisable to use the words convex or concave.  Rather refer to the edge or
            part of the trapezium that is above or below the curve.
entries.limit: Reported cohort difficulty; not diagnosis of an individual learner and not an invented distractor rationale

entries.summary: Composite trig differentiation needs chain rule; later reverse integration is separate
entries.verbatim_extracted_excerpt:
Most candidates failed to realize they had to use the chain rule to differentiate
            tan2x.  Many candidates just replaced the tan2x by sec2x. Some candidates used the identity
